headline_marked: Expulsion from party: [[Gazi Nazrul may retain MP seat]] despite viral video scandal
headline: Expulsion from party: Gazi Nazrul may retain MP seat despite viral video scandal
summary: Experts say party expulsion doesn't automatically vacate a parliamentary seat, though the Election Commission may eventually decide on 'moral turpitude'.
details: Satkhira-4 lawmaker Gazi Nazrul Islam was expelled from Jamaat-e-Islami after video clips showing him and a young woman in an intimate setting went viral, sparking nationwide reactions.
Constitution and parliamentary affairs experts told The Daily Star that expulsion from a political party does not automatically make an MP's seat vacant.
Eminent lawyer Shahdeen Malik noted that if expulsion alone led to loss of a seat, party leadership would have absolute power over lawmakers, potentially disrupting parliamentary democracy.

Under Article 70 of the constitution, a seat is vacated if an MP resigns from their party or votes against it in parliament. Since Nazrul was expelled and did not resign, experts say he may continue as an independent MP.
However, the issue of 'moral turpitude' under Article 66(1)(d) could be a factor, but this requires a court conviction and a prison sentence of at least two years.
To resolve the dispute over whether Nazrul is disqualified, the Speaker must refer the matter to the Election Commission, whose decision will be final.
The Parliament Secretariat's Secretary Golam Sorwar Bhuiyan stated that as of yesterday, parliament had not yet received formal communication from Jamaat regarding the expulsion.
caption:
Can a lawmaker keep their seat after being expelled for a viral scandal? Experts say yes.

Satkhira-4 lawmaker Gazi Nazrul Islam was expelled from Jamaat-e-Islami after video clips showing him and a young woman in an intimate setting went viral, sparking nationwide reactions.

Constitution and parliamentary affairs experts told The Daily Star that expulsion from a political party does not automatically make an MP's seat vacant.

Eminent lawyer Shahdeen Malik noted that if expulsion alone led to loss of a seat, party leadership would have absolute power over lawmakers, potentially disrupting parliamentary democracy.

Under Article 70 of the constitution, a seat is vacated if an MP resigns from their party or votes against it in parliament. Since Nazrul was expelled and did not resign, experts say he may continue as an independent MP.

However, the issue of 'moral turpitude' under Article 66(1)(d) could be a factor, but this requires a court conviction and a prison sentence of at least two years.

To resolve the dispute over whether Nazrul is disqualified, the Speaker must refer the matter to the Election Commission, whose decision will be final.

The Parliament Secretariat's Secretary Golam Sorwar Bhuiyan stated that as of yesterday, parliament had not yet received formal communication from Jamaat regarding the expulsion.

headline_marked: FIFA announces [[World Cup Best XI]], Messi and Mbappe own spots
headline: FIFA announces World Cup Best XI, Messi and Mbappe own spots
summary: Spain and France lead the squad with three players each, while Cape Verde's Vojiniya secures the top spot as the highest-voted goalkeeper.
details: FIFA has announced the tournament's Best XI, selected by fan voting. Spain and France have the most representation with three players each in the final squad.
Cape Verde's Vojiniya takes the spot in goal, becoming one of the tournament's biggest surprises. He received the highest percentage of votes overall at 39.6%.
The defense consists of Spain's Pedro Porro and Marc Cucurella, Argentina's Lisandro Martinez, and France's Dayot Upamecano. Cucurella played every minute of the tournament and provided two assists.

In the midfield, Spain's Rodri, who also won the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player, joins France's Michael Olise and England's Jude Bellingham. Olise recorded seven assists, while Bellingham scored seven goals.

The attack is led by Argentina's Lionel Messi, France's Kylian Mbappe, and Norway's Erling Haaland. Mbappe, the all-time leading goalscorer in World Cup history, won the Golden Boot with 10 goals and four assists.

Lionel Messi, at 39, played a key role in leading Argentina to the final, contributing 8 goals and 4 assists. Erling Haaland also made the mark with seven goals despite Norway's exit in the round of 16.
caption:
Who made the cut? FIFA's fan-voted Best XI is finally here, featuring the world's most dominant players.

FIFA has announced the tournament's Best XI, selected by fan voting. Spain and France have the most representation with three players each in the final squad.

Cape Verde's Vojiniya takes the spot in goal, becoming one of the tournament's biggest surprises. He received the highest percentage of votes overall at 39.6%.

The defense consists of Spain's Pedro Porro and Marc Cucurella, Argentina's Lisandro Martinez, and France's Dayot Upamecano. Cucurella played every minute of the tournament and provided two assists.

In the midfield, Spain's Rodri, who also won the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player, joins France's Michael Olise and England's Jude Bellingham. Olise recorded seven assists, while Bellingham scored seven goals.

The attack is led by Argentina's Lionel Messi, France's Kylian Mbappe, and Norway's Erling Haaland. Mbappe, the all-time leading goalscorer in World Cup history, won the Golden Boot with 10 goals and four assists.

Lionel Messi, at 39, played a key role in leading Argentina to the final, contributing 8 goals and 4 assists. Erling Haaland also made the mark with seven goals despite Norway's exit in the round of 16.
